en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ekasaññaka Hatthivagga 4 I was a caravan leader, a merchant, traveling along the road. At that time, I saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, who had arrived at the city of Sāvatthī. Having seen him, I approached the Teacher, and having approached, I paid homage to the Tathāgata. Then, having paid homage to the Tathāgata, I sat down to one side. As I sat there to one side, the Teacher preached the Dhamma to me. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. Having attained the fruit of stream-entry, I departed from that place. After departing from that place, I went to my own home. There, I summoned my sons and said this: "Come, my dear sons, listen to my words. This Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has appeared in the world. He is preaching the Dhamma, which is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the correct meaning and phrasing; he reveals the holy life that is perfectly complete and pure. It would be well for us to go forth under that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. My sons, having heard my words, said this to me: "We will do so, father. Then, together with my sons, I went to the Teacher’s presence. Having approached the Teacher, I paid homage to the Tathāgata. Then, having paid homage to the Tathāgata, I sat down to one side. As I sat there to one side, the Teacher preached the Dhamma to me. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. Having attained the fruit of stream-entry, I went forth under the Teacher. Having gone forth, I practiced the holy life under the Teacher, the Blessed One. Having practiced the holy life under the Teacher, I attained final Nibbāna. By means of this wholesome deed, having passed away from here, I was reborn in the Brahmā world. From there, passing away from that state, I was reborn in the human world. In every birth, I possessed mindfulness, and I never forgot it. Therefore, I am known as Ekasaññaka. Seeing a rag-robe clinging to the path,
he paid homage to the Teacher with palms joined in reverence.
I paid homage to the rag-robe. Because of that,
in the thirty-first aeon from now,
I do not know a miserable rebirth;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
I was once a lord of men,
a wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Ekasaññaka spoke these verses.
This is the fourth legend of the elder Ekasaññaka.
